question.:question/problem:
For the following functions, both gradients are supplied:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y)&=- 2 x - 2 y, \\ \nabla f&=-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j \\ g(x,y)&=2 x + y, \\ \nabla g&=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j
\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\nabla(fg)=g\nabla f+f\nabla g$. Which expression gives $\nabla(fg)$? You do not need to expand the products.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&(2 x + y)(-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j) \\ &{}+(- 2 x - 2 y)(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&(2 x + y)(-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j) \\ &{}-(- 2 x - 2 y)(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&-(2 x + y)(-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j) \\ &{}+(- 2 x - 2 y)(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&(- 2 x - 2 y)(-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j) \\ &{}+(2 x + y)(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}&(2 x + y)(-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j) \\ &{}+(2 x + y)(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z)$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y,z)&=- 2 x y z, \\ g(x,y,z)&=\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Work where $- 4 x y z > 0$.

\begin{aligned}&- 2 y z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf i \\ &{}- 2 x z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf j \\ &{}- 2 x y \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf k\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}&2 y z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} - 2\right)\mathbf i \\ &{}+2 x z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} - 2\right)\mathbf j \\ &{}+2 x y \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} - 2\right)\mathbf k\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}&2 y z \left(1 - 2 \ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)}\right)\mathbf i \\ &{}+2 x z \left(1 - 2 \ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)}\right)\mathbf j \\ &{}+2 x y \left(1 - 2 \ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)}\right)\mathbf k\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}&- 4 y z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf i \\ &{}- 4 x z \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf j \\ &{}- 4 x y \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y z \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf k\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y)$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y)&=- \arctan{\left(\frac{2 x}{y} \right)}, \\ \nabla f&=- \frac{2 y}{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}\mathbf i+\frac{2 x}{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}\mathbf j \\ g(x,y)&=\sqrt{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}, \\ \nabla g&=\frac{4 x}{\sqrt{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}}\mathbf i+\frac{y}{\sqrt{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}}\mathbf j
\end{aligned}
$$

Assume $y\ne0$.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{aligned}&- \frac{2 \left(2 x \arctan{\left(\frac{2 x}{y} \right)} + y\right)}{\sqrt{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}}\mathbf i \\ &{}+\frac{2 x - y \arctan{\left(\frac{2 x}{y} \right)}}{\sqrt{4 x^{2} + y^{2}}}\mathbf j\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y)$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y)&=- 2 x^{2} y - 2 x y^{2}, \\ \nabla f&=(- 4 x y - 2 y^{2})\mathbf i+(- 2 x^{2} - 4 x y)\mathbf j \\ g(x,y)&=\frac{1}{x y}, \\ \nabla g&=- \frac{1}{x^{2} y}\mathbf i- \frac{1}{x y^{2}}\mathbf j
\end{aligned}
$$

Assume $x\ne0$, $y\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the **product rule**: $\nabla(fg)=g\nabla f+f\nabla g$. Multiply each gradient by the other scalar function.

Now collect each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{x}&=g f_{x}+f g_{x} \\ &=\left(\frac{1}{x y}\right)(- 4 x y - 2 y^{2}) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x^{2} y - 2 x y^{2})\left(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y}\right) \\ &=- \frac{2 \left(2 x + y\right)}{x} \\ &\quad+\left(\frac{2 \left(x + y\right)}{x}\right) \\ &=-2
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{y}&=g f_{y}+f g_{y} \\ &=\left(\frac{1}{x y}\right)(- 2 x^{2} - 4 x y) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x^{2} y - 2 x y^{2})\left(- \frac{1}{x y^{2}}\right) \\ &=- \frac{2 \left(x + 2 y\right)}{y} \\ &\quad+\left(\frac{2 \left(x + y\right)}{y}\right) \\ &=-2
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the gradient is

$$
-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j
$$

Collect the contributions to each coordinate separately.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: -2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j
-2\mathbf j
-2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j
2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j
-4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j

$$

$$

(\nabla(fg))_{x}&=g f_{x}+f g_{x} \\ &=(\ln{\left(- 4 x y \right)})(- 2 y) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x y)\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\ &=- 2 y \ln{\left(- 4 x y \right)} \\ &\quad+(- 2 y) \\ &=- 2 y \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y \right)} + 1\right)

\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}&- 2 y \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf i \\ &{}- 2 x \left(\ln{\left(- 4 x y \right)} + 1\right)\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the contributions to each coordinate separately.

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y)$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y)&=- 2 x - 2 y + 2, \\ \nabla f&=-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j \\ g(x,y)&=\ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)}, \\ \nabla g&=- \frac{2}{- 2 x - 2 y + 2}\mathbf i- \frac{2}{- 2 x - 2 y + 2}\mathbf j
\end{aligned}
$$

Work where $- 2 x - 2 y + 2 > 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the **product rule**: $\nabla(fg)=g\nabla f+f\nabla g$. Multiply each gradient by the other scalar function.

Now collect each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{x}&=g f_{x}+f g_{x} \\ &=(\ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)})(-2) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x - 2 y + 2)\left(- \frac{2}{- 2 x - 2 y + 2}\right) \\ &=- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} \\ &\quad+(-2) \\ &=- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} - 2
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{y}&=g f_{y}+f g_{y} \\ &=(\ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)})(-2) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x - 2 y + 2)\left(- \frac{2}{- 2 x - 2 y + 2}\right) \\ &=- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} \\ &\quad+(-2) \\ &=- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} - 2
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}&(- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} - 2)\mathbf i \\ &{}+(- 2 \ln{\left(- 2 x - 2 y + 2 \right)} - 2)\mathbf j\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient Using the Properties of the Gradient

question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the **product rule**: $\nabla(fg)=g\nabla f+f\nabla g$. Multiply each gradient by the other scalar function.

Now collect each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{x}&=g f_{x}+f g_{x} \\ &=(2 x^{2} y^{2})(- 4 x) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x^{2} - 2 y)(4 x y^{2}) \\ &=- 8 x^{3} y^{2} \\ &\quad+(- 8 x y^{2} \left(x^{2} + y\right)) \\ &=- 8 x y^{2} \left(2 x^{2} + y\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla(fg))_{y}&=g f_{y}+f g_{y} \\ &=(2 x^{2} y^{2})(-2) \\ &\quad+(- 2 x^{2} - 2 y)(4 x^{2} y) \\ &=- 4 x^{2} y^{2} \\ &\quad+(- 8 x^{2} y \left(x^{2} + y\right)) \\ &=- 4 x^{2} y \left(2 x^{2} + 3 y\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the gradient is

$$
- 8 x y^{2} \left(2 x^{2} + y\right)\mathbf i- 4 x^{2} y \left(2 x^{2} + 3 y\right)\mathbf j
$$

Collect the contributions to each coordinate separately.
